verdicts.reason: Must-read CLIENT01 plate is clipped by the left frame edge in _a ('LIENT01') and _c ('T01') and in 4 of 6 strip tiles; only _b shows it whole. Caption 'Secure RDP connection' reads cleanly but is ~12 px cap height at 960x540. No private key exists yet.

Amber pulse is clear and is the focal subject. Host plates are tiny (rdp01 ~7 px cap) and WEB01 / portal.1sn0s.lab plates overlap each other in _a and _b. The rdp01 plate sits at the top edge in _c. Caption has speckle on the glyphs.
rdp01.1sn0s.lab plate is readable. The amber channel and a dark blotch run through the caption plate in _a and _b ('needs a trusted'). The 1SN0S.LAB plate is cut by the top edge in _c.

Must-read tags collide. In _b the 'Unverified' plate sits on top of 'Self-signed', leaving 'f-signed'. In _c the tags shrink to ~4 px cap, below the 18 px 1080p minimum. The 'Self-signed' tag in _a straddles the pale card and the server body. The caption has speckle damage.
RDPAuth is must-read but is tiny in _a and _b. In _c and in B-03.1 the rdp01.1sn0s.lab plate overlaps the RDPAuth text and badge. Caption is gone by _b, which is correct.

RDPAuth text is cut by the rdp01 plate in _b and _c. Key pair forms as a bulbous-bow private key and a thin-ring public key, both white and out of the container. Caption speckle is visible. Key location: private key floating beside the plate and not in the container (_c, strip tiles 5 and 6).

The white key shape floats at upper right beside the public-key plate in all 6 strip tiles and in _a, _b and _c. It never enters the closed safe container below it. The beat is 'Private key anchored' but no frame shows it anchored in the container. A key outside its container is a key violation (F-03).

The key is still outside the container in _a and strip tile 1, right beside the public-key plate and where the capsule appears. It then disappears; no tile shows it entering the container. A key shape beside or near the capsule counts as a violation. The caption 'The request is signed, not the key sent' is speckled.

Beam from the safe to the capsule is clear and the capsule does not move. The private key is not visible in any tile, so it cannot be located. It is presumably inside the closed safe but never shown there. Caption glyphs are damaged and the caption fades out in the last tile.

AD plate is clipped by the top edge in _b. The rdp01 plate is large and noisy. RDPAuth, a must-read in this beat, is hidden behind the rdp01 plate in _b and _c. A white ring-shaped key bow hangs inside the server above the container in _b, _c and strip tiles 2 to 6 and is not in the container. The capsule sits outside the server beside AD.

Capsule travels along the lit cyan route. The CA 1 nameplate is tiny until _c. The ring-shaped key bow remains visible inside the server door in strip tiles 1 and 2, outside the container. The caption appears only in the last tile and is speckled.

The four check lines are not readable. The 1SN0S Issuing CA 1 nameplate covers 'Requester authenticated'. The capsule covers the start of 'Enroll permission granted'. The key module covers 'Request meets template policy', which is cut at 'templ'. Cyan text sits on a cyan wall. The caption reads 'venfies' because of glyph damage.

Card SAN and EKU fields ('rdp01.1sn0s.lab', 'Remote Desktop Authentication') are ~6 px cap, detached below the card. They are overlapped by the left-over check list and the nameplate and are unreadable. Caption speckled and absent in _c.

The card fields are chopped by the server door ('Remote', 'top Authentication') and overlap each other. The two cards are indistinguishable at this size, so the copy of the CA certificate cannot be read. A ring-shaped key bow and a thin white pill remain inside the server above the container in every tile.

The '1SN0S Root CA' label is plain white text over the gold plinth with no plate. A dark rectangle cuts through the letters and a ghost engraving sits behind them. White on gold is roughly 1.5:1, so the must-read fails L-02. The vault is clear and cable-free.

The flashback tags 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony' and 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' are ~5 to 7 px cap. In strip tile 2 they overprint the CA 1 nameplate and check list and cannot be read. The caption plate is washed out against the desaturated bright scene in _a. The CA request capsule is not readable as distinct from the earlier request.

Root label is the same unplated white-on-gold text, and ~5 px in the pulled-back frames. The gold link is clear. The caption 'The Root CA is the trust anchor' is speckled and fades over scene detail in the last tile.

The wide frames make every label ~4 px cap. The card fields 'rdp01.1sn0s.lab / Remote Desktop Authentication' float beside the user at ~6 px, detached from the cards. No handshake-proof impression shape is identifiable in any tile. The key is not visible; location unknown.

The required caption 'The client validates the whole chain' is rendered so damaged it reads 'The cllent vaiidates the whote chain' (_a, _b, _c). In _a the CLIENT01 plate overlaps the cards. The 'Installed earlier by policy' tag is readable in _b.

The two AIA tags overlap the intermediate card and CLIENT01 plate. They are clipped on the left in _c ('issing intermediate') and sit outside title-safe in strip tiles 5 and 6. The 'Remote Desktop Au_hentication' field is chopped by the card. The caption is nearly unreadable.

The checklist is drawn huge and tilted over the cards and user. It is clipped at the right edge in _b ('trusted ro') and strip tile 3. Tick glyphs overprint the first letter of each line ('Chain', 'Signatures', 'Currently'). It shrinks to ~6 px cap in tile 6. The caption is damaged and the CLIENT01 plate is partly hidden.

The checklist is ~5 to 6 px cap and tilted. 'OCSP if deployed' touches the 'Revocation OK' line and the first glyph reads as J. The amber CRL fetch is a long channel on the floor and is hard to tell from the pending channel.

The required caption 'Trusted RDP connection established' is unreadable (letters broken, reads 'establisned'). In _c the checklist runs off the right edge ('Name matches rdp01.1sn0s.l'). The mint-green channel against salmon-amber relies on hue alone.

The WEB01 and portal.1sn0s.lab plates overlap each other and the WebServer-TLS badge text, which is a must-read for this beat and shows only 'LS'. The rdp01 plate overlaps RDPAuth in _a. The labels are readable otherwise.

In _a and strip tiles 2, 3 and 4 the web server's private key (white ring and key) floats outside the safe container. In tile 4 it sits directly under the request capsule. It then vanishes without ever being shown inside the container. Key outside container is a violation.

Eligibility tags are cut off by the top edge in _a and stack over the CA 2 nameplate in _b and _c. 'WebServer-TLS not published here' is clipped and overlapped by the 1SN0S.LAB plate. The WEB01 and portal plates overlap and tilt, hiding the WebServer-TLS badge. The caption is speckled and overlaps the web server base in _c.

The capsule route to CA 2 is clear. The WEB01 and portal plates plus the caption sit on the web server at the capsule's origin in _a and _b. The caption glyphs are damaged and the key location is not visible.

The CA 2 nameplate covers 'Requester authenticated'. The capsule covers 'Enroll permission granted'. 'Name supplied in request - enrollment restricted' prints over 'Request meets template policy' (garbled) and is cut off ('enrollmen', 'restric'). The checks are not readable.

The caption 'Issuing CA 2 signs the TLS certificate' reads 'Signs the 7LS certificate'. The card fields are tiny, detached and chopped ('Aut_entication'). In _c and strip tile 6 the WEB01/portal plate grows to cover the top third of the frame and the interior.

In _a the WEB01 label fills the lower half of the frame and hides the CA 2 vault, the focal subject. In _b and _c the labels are 3 to 5 px and the CA 2 nameplate is truncated ('1SN0S Issuing'). The gold links are clear.

_a, _b and _c show no readable check labels. Only strip tiles 4 to 6 do, with 'Name matches portal.1sn0s.lab' and 'EKU permits TLS server auth' clipped at the right edge and overlapping 'Currently valid' and the cards. portal.1sn0s.lab under the chair is chopped. The checks cannot be read in the sampled frames.

The hero-shot labels are ~3 to 4 px and the root label is crossed by the trust link. No host or CA names can be read. In _a the caption 'Different issuing paths. One trusted root.' sits over the AD pillar and the cyan link, and it is damaged by speckle.

The title card 'Certificate Flow - From request to trust' is clean and readable (cap ~14 px at 960x540, just under the 15 px floor). It covers the CA vaults while the scene fades. The final frame is black, which is an intended clean end.

findings.evidence: Required captions are drawn with speckle and ghost-fringe damage across the glyphs, so letters break up. 'The client validates the whole chain' reads 'The cllent vaiidates the whote chain'. 'Trusted RDP connection established' reads 'establisned'. 'Issuing CA 1 verifies' reads 'venfies'. 'Signs the TLS certificate' reads 'Signs the 7LS certificate'. Worst in B-06.2 to B-06.6 and B-08.2. Frames B-01.1 and B-09.3 show the same caption font clean, so this is a compositing defect. The packet has no sampled contrast measurement to test against.
findings.why: Required captions are the only narration. When two of the S6 captions cannot be read, the viewer cannot follow the validation or the established session. This is an unreadable required caption, a BLOCKER by the severity definition.
findings.direction: Composite the caption layer after grain, DOF and noise, with a solid plate and clean anti-aliased text, so every required caption reads at full legibility on every frame. Re-measure caption contrast on the final frame.

findings.evidence: The white private-key shape floats at the upper right, beside the public-key plate, in all 6 strip tiles of B-03.2, in _a to _c, and in the first tile of B-03.3. It never enters the closed safe container below it, then disappears. From B-04.1 on, a ring-shaped key bow and a thin white pill hang inside the server above the container (B-04.1_b, B-04.5_b). In B-07.2_a and strip tile 4 the web server key sits outside its container, directly under the request capsule, and then vanishes.
findings.why: A stored private key must stay in its locked container. A key outside it, beside the capsule, or one that cannot be located afterwards is a key violation. A viewer cannot tell where the key is, or that it ever reached the container, so the central message 'private key stays on the server' is contradicted by the picture.
findings.direction: Show each private key travelling into, and sealed inside, its own locked container, with a visible lock-and-anchor moment. Keep a key-shaped glyph only inside the container for the rest of the film. The key must never be near the capsule, and the container must read as occupied.

findings.evidence: At 960x540 the caption text is about 9.7 px per character with ~12 px capital height (the 'Secure RDP connection' plate is about 203 px wide for 21 characters). The spec minimum is 15 px at 960x540. The title card is ~14 px. In-world must-read labels measure 4 to 9 px: 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony', 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request', the root label in wide shots, card SAN/EKU fields, check lists in B-06.5/B-06.6, and the hero shot names. The 18 px (9 px at 960) minimum is missed. No measured bounds are supplied in the packet, so these are measured from the images.
findings.why: Captions at 80% of the minimum and must-read labels at 25 to 50% of it fail L-01. Narration and names cannot be read at normal viewing size.
findings.direction: Raise caption type to at least 15 px cap at 960x540 (30 px at 1080p). Hold every must-read label at 9 px or more at 960x540 for its whole moment, by scaling it or moving the camera in.

findings.evidence: The four CA check lines are hidden. The 1SN0S Issuing CA 1 nameplate sits over 'Requester authenticated'. The capsule sits over 'Enroll permission granted'. The key module is over the end of 'Request meets template policy', which is cut to 'templ'. Cyan text sits on a cyan wall. In B-08.1 the 'Name supplied in request - enrollment restricted' note prints directly on 'Request meets template policy', producing garbled text. It is clipped by the vault at 'enrollmen' and 'restric'. The check list is left over in the CA 1 vault in the flashback B-05.2.
findings.why: The four checks and the CA 2 note are the PKI content of these beats and must be at least 90% unoccluded for 1.5 s. None reaches that.
findings.direction: Lay the four checks out in a clear column in front of the vault, on a plate, facing the camera. Keep the nameplate, capsule and module off them. Put the CA 2 note on its own line. Clear the check list before the flashback.

findings.evidence: The certificate field text ('rdp01.1sn0s.lab', 'Remote Desktop Authentication', 'portal.1sn0s.lab', 'Server Authentication') is ~6 px cap and is not on the card but floats below or beside it, detached. It is chopped by the server door ('Remote', 'top Authentication'), by cards and desks ('Aut_entication'), and overlapped by other text. In B-06.x it is the only place the certificate names are visible.
findings.why: SAN and EKU are must-read in B-04.4 and B-08.2, and the SAN/EKU identity is what the name-match check relies on. The viewer cannot read either.
findings.direction: Print the SAN, EKU and validity on the face of the card, large enough to read at 9 px cap or more at 960x540, and keep them unoccluded while the card is the focal subject.

findings.evidence: The validation checklist is a large block of text tilted well over 35 degrees to the camera and drawn on top of the cards and user. It is clipped at the right edge in B-06.4_b ('trusted ro'), B-06.6_c ('rdp01.1sn0s.l') and B-09.1 ('Name matches port', 'EKU permits TLS s'). Tick glyphs overprint the first letter of each line. In B-06.5/B-06.6 it shrinks to ~5 px cap. 'OCSP if deployed' touches the 'Revocation OK' line and reads 'JCSP'. The 6th, amber, tick is small beside the green ticks.
findings.why: The six checks are the payoff of S6. They cannot be read in full in any frame, and the chain they validate is hidden behind them.
findings.direction: Place the check list beside the chain, facing the camera within 35 degrees, inside title-safe and with a consistent size. Offset the tick glyphs from the text. Separate 'OCSP if deployed' from the Revocation line.

findings.evidence: The two AIA tags are placed across the intermediate and server cards and over the CLIENT01 plate. They are clipped on the left in _c ('issing intermediate?') and sit past x=48 inside the edge in the strip tiles. The nearer card hides part of 'Fetching never creates trust'.
findings.why: The AIA caveat is the teaching point of B-06.3 and covers the focal chain, so it is neither readable nor clear of the action.
findings.direction: Put the AIA indicator and its two tags to one side of the chain, on plates, inside title-safe and not covering the cards or CLIENT01.

findings.evidence: The WEB01 and portal.1sn0s.lab plates overlap each other and hide the WebServer-TLS badge text (only 'LS' shows). In B-07.3 they tilt and overlap the capsule route. In B-08.2_c and B-08.3_a they scale up to cover the top third and then the lower half of the frame, hiding the CA 2 vault (the focal subject of B-08.3). In B-07.3 the eligibility tags stack over the CA 2 nameplate and are cut at the top of the frame ('Template published' at y~5). 'WebServer-TLS not published here' is clipped on the left and overlapped by the 1SN0S.LAB plate.
findings.why: WebServer-TLS, the CA 2 name and the four eligibility tags are must-read in B-07.1 and B-07.3. They are occluded or cut off, so the viewer cannot see why CA 1 is ineligible and CA 2 is.
findings.direction: Give plates a fixed on-screen scale and fixed offsets so they never overlap each other or the focal object. Anchor the eligibility tags below the CA 2 nameplate with margins inside title-safe.

findings.evidence: In-world text is clipped or lies outside the 90% title-safe area (x 48 to 912, y 27 to 513 at 960x540). Examples: CLIENT01 cut at the left ('LIENT01', 'T01'); the AD '1SN0S.LAB' plate touches or crosses the top edge; the rdp01 plate sits at y~12 to 40; the AIA tags are clipped at the left; the check lists run off the right edge; the eligibility tags start at y~5; the WEB01 plate runs off the right.
findings.why: Text outside title-safe can be cut by a broadcast overscan or by the edge of the frame. Several must-read labels lose letters.
findings.direction: Keep every must-read label's bounds inside title-safe for its whole on-screen time, by framing the camera or constraining label placement.

findings.evidence: The root label '1SN0S Root CA' is plain white text with no plate, drawn over the gold-yellow plinth. A dark vertical rectangle cuts through the letters and a ghost engraved copy shows behind them. In the pulled-back B-05.3, B-06.x, B-07.x and B-09.2 frames it is 3 to 5 px and the trust link runs through it (B-09.2).
findings.why: Root CA is the must-read subject of B-05.1. White text on gold is roughly 1.5:1, far below the 4.5:1 minimum, so the trust-anchor name cannot be read.
findings.direction: Put the root name on the same dark plate used elsewhere, remove the occluding rectangle and ghost text, keep the trust link off the name, and keep it at least 9 px cap.

findings.evidence: In the flashback the tag 'Issuing CA 1's own CA request' (the must-read that keeps the CA request separate from the RDP request) is ~5 px cap and 'Earlier: offline signing ceremony' is ~7 px. In strip tile 2 both print on the CA 1 nameplate and the left-over check text. The caption plate is pale and washed out over the desaturated bright scene in _a. The CA=true band on the request is not visible.
findings.why: The accuracy constraint for B-05.2 depends on the viewer reading that this is the CA's own request. It cannot be read at this size and with this collision.
findings.direction: Enlarge and isolate both flashback tags on plates, clear of other text, and keep the CA=true band and tag visible for the whole carry.

findings.evidence: The caption plate (y 455 to 503 at 960x540) sits over the focal action in several frames: over the web server base and the capsule route (B-07.3_c, B-07.4_a, B-07.4_b), over the AD pillar and the cyan trust link (B-09.2_a, B-09.2_b), over the user's chair and desk (B-06.3_b), and over the safe's lower edge (B-03.4_c). Captions sit at a fixed lower position regardless of the framing.
findings.why: The caption must not intersect the focal subject's projected bounding box, but camera framing pushes the subject into the caption band.
findings.direction: Frame the focal subject above the caption band, or move the caption to a clear band for these beats, and re-check the intersection on every frame of the hold.

findings.evidence: The packet carries no palette-check results, CIEDE2000 values or colour-vision-deficiency simulations, so L-07 cannot be verified. From the images: pending amber is rendered as a pink-salmon, validated green as pale mint. The 6th check's tick is a small amber dot beside teal-green ticks. The CRL fetch and the pending channel are both salmon. These warm and light-green hues are the pair most prone to confusion under deuteranopia and protanopia, and the tick sizes give no second cue.
findings.why: Required measurement is absent, and the visible colour pairs are risky, so pending versus validated cannot be shown to be distinguishable.
findings.direction: Supply the measured role-colour samples and the CVD results for all eight roles. Add a shape or luminance cue to pending versus validated ticks and channels.

findings.evidence: In B-02.2_b the 'Unverified' plate sits on the 'Self-signed' tag, leaving 'f-signed'. In _c both are ~4 px. In B-02.3_c and B-03.1_a to _c the rdp01.1sn0s.lab plate covers the RDPAuth text.
findings.why: 'Self-signed', 'Unverified' and 'RDPAuth' are must-read labels. They overlap each other or are too small for the 1.5 s hold.
findings.direction: Offset the two client tags vertically and keep the server plate clear of the template badge text.

findings.evidence: The amber channel passes through the caption plate, and a darker rectangle shows behind it, in B-02.1 and B-02.2. The caption text is partly overprinted ('needs a trusted').
findings.why: The plate is not opaque enough to keep the text clear of scene detail behind it.
findings.direction: Use an opaque or heavily dimmed plate and keep scene objects out of the caption band.
